title: Checking a missing key with `in` adds it to `bucket`'s keys
spec:
This is the more-itertools library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 run_tests.py`.

A failed lookup on a `bucket` leaves a phantom key behind, so the object reports a key that no item ever had.

```python
import more_itertools as mi
D = mi.bucket([10, 20, 11, 21], key=lambda x: 10 * (x // 10))
30 in D        # False, as expected
sorted(D)      # expected [10, 20], actual [10, 20, 30]
```

Selecting an absent bucket does the same: after `list(D[30])` (which correctly gives `[]`), `sorted(D)` is `[10, 20, 30]` instead of `[10, 20]`. It also happens when a `validator` accepts the missing key, and every miss adds one more key.

Iterating a bucket should only ever report keys for which at least one item was actually seen, no matter how many `in` tests or lookups were done before. Keys whose items were already consumed through `D[key]` should still be listed, as now.
acceptance: `in` tests and lookups of missing keys never change the reported keys, with or without a validator
Keys of items already consumed through selection are still reported
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
